title: Truly Scale-Equivariant Deep Nets with Fourier Layers

en.text: A cat is a cat whether it fills the frame or sits far away as a handful of pixels. We would like a vision network to behave the same way: shrink the object, and the features should shrink with it, while the predicted label stays put. This property is called scale-equivariance, and a line of scale-equivariant CNNs has pursued it by sharing weights across a bank of resized kernels. The catch is subtle but consequential. These methods are derived on paper in the continuous domain and only later discretized for a real, pixel-grid implementation, and that discretization step leaks. What comes out is a network that is approximately scale-equivariant, carrying a small but stubborn error that never quite reaches zero.

A NeurIPS 2023 paper from Purdue University argues that the residual error is not a tuning problem but a modeling one. Down-scaling a discrete signal is a signal-processing operation, and signal processing has a hard rule for it: before you throw away samples, you must low-pass filter, or high frequencies fold down into low ones and corrupt the result. The continuous-domain formulations simply had no place for that anti-aliasing filter. The paper's fix is to formulate down-scaling directly in the discrete domain, with anti-aliasing built in from the first line, and then to rebuild every network component as a Fourier layer that respects it. The payoff is a family of deep nets that is truly scale-equivariant, with an end-to-end equivariance error of exactly zero, by construction rather than by luck.

en.caption: Figure 1. Why ordinary CNNs are only approximately scale-equivariant. Feed a high-resolution digit and its ideally down-scaled version through the same CNN and the two feature maps disagree (top vs. bottom, red cross). The property we actually want is the reverse: down-scaling a high-resolution feature should recover exactly the feature computed from the low-resolution input. Building a network where that holds is the paper's goal.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02922  |  Code: https://github.com/ashiq24/Scale_Equivarinat_Fourier_Layer
The problem: equivariance that isn't quite exact

Scale-equivariance means that if you resize the input, the network's internal features transform in the corresponding way and the final label is unchanged. Recent scale-equivariant networks, such as SESN, DSS, and DISCO, chase this by weight-sharing across scales: the same kernel, resized, is applied at each scale. Derived in the continuous domain, the idea is clean. But real images live on a discrete grid, so the continuous kernels have to be sampled, and that sampling reintroduces exactly the aliasing the continuous math never had to worry about. The result is a measurable equivariance error, on the order of a few tenths in the paper's tables, which means the guarantee these methods advertise holds only approximately.

The paper's diagnosis is that the missing ingredient is anti-aliasing. The Nyquist sampling theorem says that when you subsample a discrete signal, you must first remove the frequencies that the coarser grid can no longer represent; skip that step and those high frequencies alias into low ones, the same effect that makes wagon wheels spin backwards on film. Because prior work down-scaled in the continuous domain, there was no natural place to insert this filter. Getting it wrong is precisely what produces the residual error.
The idea: define down-scaling correctly, then obey one frequency rule

The authors start by pinning down what down-scaling should mean. They define it as ideal downsampling: first apply an ideal low-pass filter that zeros out every frequency above the new grid's Nyquist limit, then subsample. Figure 2 shows this filtering as a pointwise product in the frequency domain, where the filter keeps a band of low frequencies and discards the rest. With this definition in hand, the anti-aliasing is no longer an afterthought bolted onto a continuous derivation; it is the very definition of the operation the network must be equivariant to.

en.caption: Figure 2. Ideal downsampling as frequency-domain filtering. The signal spectrum X is multiplied pointwise by an ideal low-pass filter H that is 1 on a band of low frequencies and 0 elsewhere, leaving only the retained low frequencies (H ⊙ X). Removing the high frequencies before subsampling is exactly the anti-aliasing step that prior continuous-domain formulations had no place for.

en.text: From this definition the paper derives its central condition, stated as Claim 1: a deep net is scale-equivariant under ideal downsampling if and only if every output frequency depends only on input frequencies that are equal or lower. Intuitively, information may flow from low frequencies up to high ones but never the other way, so that discarding the high band commutes with running the layer. This single rule, one output frequency reads only equal-or-lower input frequencies, becomes the design constraint that every layer must satisfy.
Rebuilding the network as Fourier layers

Enforcing the frequency rule means redesigning each standard component. The convolution becomes a spatially-local Fourier layer: it operates in the frequency domain but constrains its kernel so the learned features stay spatially local, keeping the useful inductive bias of a CNN while obeying the dependency structure. The non-linearity is applied band by band so it does not mix a high frequency back into a low one. Pooling is likewise re-expressed in the Fourier domain to preserve the same structure. On top of this equivariant feature extractor sits a per-scale classifier that predicts once at every scale while sharing a single MLP across scales through Fourier zero-padding. Because every operation runs in the Fourier domain, a layer costs on the order of |A| N log N + K N, keeping the whole design practical.

One more piece ties prediction quality to scale. The authors add a hinge consistency loss that penalizes the model whenever a higher-resolution image is predicted worse than its own down-scaled version. The intuition is simple: more resolution should never hurt, so the loss nudges the higher-resolution prediction to be at least as good as the coarser one, encouraging scale-consistent behavior on top of the exact equivariance the architecture already guarantees.
Results: exactly zero error, and it helps most where it is hardest

The model is evaluated on the two standard scale-equivariance benchmarks, MNIST-scale (resolutions from 8×8 up to 28×28) and STL10-scale (48 up to 97), against baselines including SESN, DSS, SI-CovNet, SS-CNN, DISCO, and a plain Fourier CNN. On MNIST-scale under ideal downsampling with all scales, it reaches 0.9889 accuracy and 0.9716 scale-consistency, the best on every metric, and, crucially, an equivariance error of exactly 0.00 where strong baselines like DISCO still register around 0.44. The zero is not a rounding artifact; it is guaranteed by the construction.

en.caption: Table 1. MNIST-scale accuracy, scale-consistency, and equivariance error under ideal downsampling (all scales). The proposed model leads on every metric, and its equivariance error is exactly zero by construction while the strongest baselines retain a measurable residual.

en.text: The advantage widens on the harder benchmark. On STL10-scale, natural color images where approximate methods struggle, the model reaches 0.7332 accuracy against 0.5844 for the next-best Fourier CNN, a gain of roughly 15 points, again with zero equivariance error. It also degrades gracefully under non-ideal downsampling, where the anti-aliasing filter is imperfect and Gibbs ringing appears: even there it stays the best model at 0.9880 accuracy, 0.9760 scale-consistency, and a small 0.05 error. And it is the most data-efficient of the group, reaching 0.9606 accuracy with just 1,000 training samples on MNIST-scale versus DISCO's 0.9457.

A feature visualization gives a sense of what the equivariant layers actually learn. Across both ideal and non-ideal downsampling, the model's feature maps trace spatially local structure, the contours and edges of each digit, rather than the diffuse, resolution-dependent patterns an ordinary CNN produces. The spatially-local Fourier convolution is doing what it was designed to do.

en.caption: Figure 3. Learned features under ideal (top rows) and non-ideal (bottom) downsampling. From the input digit the model produces feature maps that highlight spatially local structure, digit contours and edges, in both settings, evidence that the spatially-local Fourier convolution keeps a CNN-like inductive bias while remaining exactly scale-equivariant.

en.text: Ablation: the consistency loss earns its place

To check that the consistency loss is doing real work rather than riding along, the authors remove it and retrain at several training-set sizes. Both accuracy and scale-consistency drop at every size: at 5,000 samples scale-consistency falls from 0.9296 to 0.9150, and at 2,500 samples from 0.8906 to 0.8633. The loss reliably improves scale-consistent behavior, which is why it stays in the final recipe. The authors also report that applying the non-linearity directly in the frequency domain, though it preserves equivariance, hurt classification, which is why they use a spatial-domain scale-equivariant non-linearity instead.
Takeaway

The lasting lesson is to treat scale-equivariance as a signal-processing problem. Once you define down-scaling as ideal, anti-aliased downsampling and require every output frequency to read only equal-or-lower input frequencies, you can assemble a network from Fourier layers that is exactly scale-equivariant, with provably zero error instead of the small residuals that trailed earlier methods.

The guarantee is not bought with accuracy. The model matches or beats prior scale-equivariant CNNs and is markedly more data-efficient, with the largest gains showing up on the harder natural-image setting. It is worth being precise about the boundary, though: the exact-zero guarantee lives in the ideal-downsampling regime, where theory and implementation coincide. Under non-ideal downsampling, when the anti-aliasing filter is imperfect and Gibbs ringing creeps in, a small error returns, even if the model still comes out ahead of every baseline.

More broadly, the paper is a reminder that many of the "approximate" equivariances in deep learning are approximate only because a fundamentally discrete operation was modeled as if it were continuous, and then discretized after the fact. Treating the operation the network must respect as a genuine signal-processing step, with anti-aliasing built in from the start rather than patched in at the end, is what converts an approximate symmetry into an exact one. The same recipe, define the discrete operation correctly and then constrain every layer to commute with it, may well carry over to the many other transformations that deep networks are routinely asked to respect.

zh.text: 一只猫无论占满整个画面，还是远处几个像素的小点，它都还是一只猫。我们希望视觉网络也能这样：物体缩小，提取到的特征应当随之缩小，而预测出的类别保持不变。这一性质叫做尺度等变（scale-equivariance）。一类尺度等变 CNN 为此在一组不同尺寸的卷积核之间共享权重，用「同一个核、缩放到不同尺度」的方式来逼近它。问题很微妙但影响不小：这些方法是在连续域（continuous domain）里推导出来的，真正落到像素网格上实现时才做离散化，而离散化这一步会「漏」。最终得到的网络只是近似尺度等变，始终带着一个不大却顽固、怎么调都到不了零的误差。

普渡大学发表在 NeurIPS 2023 的这篇论文提出，这个残余误差不是调参问题，而是建模问题。对离散信号做降采样本质上是一次信号处理操作，而信号处理对此有一条硬规则：在丢弃采样点之前必须先做低通滤波，否则高频会「折叠」进低频、污染结果。连续域的推导里根本没有给这个抗混叠（anti-aliasing）滤波器留位置。论文的做法是：直接在离散域里定义降采样，从第一步就把抗混叠内建进去，再把网络的每一个组件都重建成遵守这条规则的 Fourier 层。回报是一族真正尺度等变的深度网络，端到端等变误差精确为零，靠的是构造本身而不是运气。

zh.caption: 图1 为什么普通 CNN 只是近似尺度等变。把一张高分辨率数字和它「理想降采样」后的版本送进同一个 CNN，得到的两张特征图并不一致（上、下两路，红叉标出）。我们真正想要的是反过来成立：对高分辨率特征做降采样，应当精确还原出直接由低分辨率输入算得的特征。构造一个满足这一点的网络，正是本文的目标。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02922  |  代码：https://github.com/ashiq24/Scale_Equivarinat_Fourier_Layer
问题：不够精确的「等变」

尺度等变的意思是：如果你缩放输入，网络的内部特征会以对应方式一起变换，而最终类别保持不变。近期的尺度等变网络，比如 SESN、DSS、DISCO，都通过跨尺度共享权重来追求这一点：同一个核缩放后作用在每个尺度上。在连续域里看，这个思路很干净。但真实图像活在离散网格上，连续核必须被采样，而这一采样又把连续数学从不需要操心的混叠（aliasing）重新引了回来。结果就是一个可测量的等变误差，在论文的表格里大约是零点几，这意味着这些方法所宣称的保证，实际上只近似成立。
论文的诊断是：缺失的关键一环是抗混叠。奈奎斯特采样定理（Nyquist sampling theorem）指出，当你对离散信号降采样时，必须先去掉更粗网格已无法表示的那些频率；跳过这一步，高频就会混叠进低频，就像电影里马车轮子看上去在倒转的那种效应。因为此前的工作是在连续域里做降采样的，就没有一个自然的位置来插入这个滤波器。而没把它处理对，恰恰就是那个残余误差的来源。
核心思路：先把降采样定义对，再服从一条频率规则
作者先把「降采样到底该是什么」钉死。他们将其定义为理想降采样（ideal downsampling）：先施加一个理想低通滤波器，把高于新网格奈奎斯特上限的所有频率清零，然后再抽样。图2 把这个滤波画成频域里的逐点相乘——滤波器保留一段低频、丢掉其余部分。有了这个定义，抗混叠就不再是补在连续推导后面的马后炮，而正是网络所要等变的那个操作的定义本身。

zh.caption: 图2 理想降采样即频域滤波。信号频谱 X 与一个理想低通滤波器 H 逐点相乘，H 在一段低频上取 1、其余处取 0，最终只留下被保留的低频（H ⊙ X）。在抽样之前先去掉高频，正是此前连续域方法无处安放的那一步抗混叠。

zh.text: 由这个定义出发，论文推导出它的核心条件，即 Claim 1：在理想降采样下，一个深度网络尺度等变，当且仅当每个输出频率只依赖于相等或更低的输入频率。直观地说，信息可以从低频流向高频，但绝不能反过来，这样一来「丢掉高频」这一步就能和「跑这一层」相交换。这条唯一的规则——一个输出频率只读取相等或更低的输入频率——就成了每一层都必须满足的设计约束。
把网络重建为 Fourier 层

要强制这条频率规则，就得把每个标准组件重新设计。卷积变成一个空间局部（spatially-local）的 Fourier 层：它在频域里运算，却约束自己的核使学到的特征保持空间局部性，从而既保留了 CNN 那份有用的归纳偏置，又服从依赖结构。非线性逐频带施加，避免把高频重新混回低频。池化同样在频域里重新表达，以保持相同的结构。在这个等变特征提取器之上，是一个逐尺度分类器（per-scale classifier），它在每个尺度各预测一次，并通过 Fourier 零填充在各尺度间共享同一个 MLP。由于所有运算都在频域进行，每层的代价约为 |A| N log N + K N，让整个设计保持实用。
还有一块拼图把预测质量和尺度绑在一起。作者加了一项 hinge 一致性损失（consistency loss），只要某张高分辨率图像被预测得比它自己降采样后的版本还差，就对模型施加惩罚。直觉很简单：更高的分辨率不该反而更差，于是这项损失促使高分辨率预测至少不弱于粗分辨率预测，在架构已经保证的精确等变之上，再鼓励出尺度一致的行为。
结果：误差精确为零，且越难的场景收益越大

模型在两个标准尺度等变基准上评测：MNIST-scale（分辨率从 8×8 到 28×28）和 STL10-scale（从 48 到 97），对比的基线包括 SESN、DSS、SI-CovNet、SS-CNN、DISCO 以及一个普通的 Fourier CNN。在理想降采样、覆盖全部尺度的 MNIST-scale 上，它取得 0.9889 的准确率和 0.9716 的尺度一致性，在每一项指标上都最好；而最关键的是，等变误差精确为 0.00，而 DISCO 这样的强基线仍有约 0.44。这个零不是四舍五入的结果，而是由构造保证的。

zh.caption: 表1 理想降采样（全部尺度）下 MNIST-scale 的准确率、尺度一致性与等变误差。本文模型在每一项指标上领先，其等变误差由构造精确为零，而最强的基线仍保留可测量的残余误差。

zh.text: 在更难的基准上，这个优势进一步拉开。在 STL10-scale 这个近似方法普遍吃力的自然彩色图像基准上，模型取得 0.7332 的准确率，而次好的 Fourier CNN 只有 0.5844，领先约 15 个百分点，且等变误差依然为零。它在非理想降采样下也退化得很平缓：当抗混叠滤波器不完美、出现 Gibbs 振铃时，它仍是最好的模型，准确率 0.9880、尺度一致性 0.9760，误差仅 0.05。它还是这组方法里最省数据的：在 MNIST-scale 上仅用 1000 个训练样本就达到 0.9606 的准确率，而 DISCO 为 0.9457。
一组特征可视化让人直观看到这些等变层到底学到了什么。无论理想还是非理想降采样，模型的特征图都勾勒出空间局部的结构——每个数字的轮廓和边缘，而不是普通 CNN 产生的那种弥散、依赖分辨率的图案。空间局部 Fourier 卷积确实在做它被设计出来要做的事。

zh.caption: 图3 理想（上方各行）与非理想（下方）降采样下学到的特征。从输入数字出发，模型在两种设定下都产生突出空间局部结构——数字轮廓与边缘——的特征图，说明空间局部 Fourier 卷积在保持精确尺度等变的同时，保留了类似 CNN 的归纳偏置。

zh.text: 消融：一致性损失确实有用

为验证一致性损失是在真正起作用、而不是搭个便车，作者把它去掉后在若干训练集规模上重训。准确率和尺度一致性在每个规模上都下降：5000 个样本时尺度一致性从 0.9296 掉到 0.9150，2500 个样本时从 0.8906 掉到 0.8633。这项损失稳定地改善了尺度一致性行为，因此保留在最终配方中。作者还指出，如果把非线性直接放到频域里施加，虽然能保持等变，却会损害分类效果，这也是他们改用空间域尺度等变非线性的原因。
结语

最值得记住的一点是：把尺度等变当作一个信号处理问题来对待。一旦你把降采样定义为理想的、带抗混叠的降采样，并要求每个输出频率只读取相等或更低的输入频率，就能用 Fourier 层拼出一个精确尺度等变的网络——误差在可证明的意义上为零，而不是像早期方法那样拖着一条小尾巴。而且这个保证并非以准确率为代价换来：模型追平或超过此前的尺度等变 CNN，并且明显更省数据，收益最大的恰是更难的自然图像场景。需要如实说明的边界是：精确为零的保证成立于理想降采样这一设定；在非理想降采样下会回来一个小误差，尽管模型依然领先。把离散信号处理这一步做对，正是把近似等变变成精确等变的关键。

zh.caption: 图1 为什么普通 CNN 只是近似尺度等变。把一张高分辨率数字和它「理想降采样」后的版本送进同一个 CNN，得到的两张特征图并不一致（上、下两路，红叉标出）。我们真正想要的是反过来成立：对高分辨率特征做降采样，应当精确还原出直接由低分辨率输入算得的特征。构造一个满足这一点的网络，正是本文的目标。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02922  |  代码：https://github.com/ashiq24/Scale_Equivarinat_Fourier_Layer

en.title: NeurIPS 2023: Making Deep Nets Truly Scale-Equivariant, With Zero Error
en.subtitle: Purdue University rebuilds every network layer in the Fourier domain so that resizing an image and running the network commute exactly, not just approximately.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 让网络对尺度变化「真正」等变，误差精确为零
zh.subtitle: 普渡大学用 Fourier 层重建每一层网络，使「缩放图像」和「跑网络」两个操作严格可交换，而不再只是近似成立

en.caption: Figure 1. Why ordinary CNNs are only approximately scale-equivariant. Feed a high-resolution digit and its ideally down-scaled version through the same CNN and the two feature maps disagree (top vs. bottom, red cross). The property we actually want is the reverse: down-scaling a high-resolution feature should recover exactly the feature computed from the low-resolution input. Building a network where that holds is the paper's goal.

en.text: The problem: equivariance that isn't quite exact

Scale-equivariance means that if you resize the input, the network's internal features transform in the corresponding way and the final label is unchanged. Recent scale-equivariant networks, such as SESN, DSS, and DISCO, chase this by weight-sharing across scales: the same kernel, resized, is applied at each scale. Derived in the continuous domain, the idea is clean. But real images live on a discrete grid, so the continuous kernels have to be sampled, and that sampling reintroduces exactly the aliasing the continuous math never had to worry about. The result is a measurable equivariance error, on the order of a few tenths in the paper's tables, which means the guarantee these methods advertise holds only approximately.

The paper's diagnosis is that the missing ingredient is anti-aliasing. The Nyquist sampling theorem says that when you subsample a discrete signal, you must first remove the frequencies that the coarser grid can no longer represent; skip that step and those high frequencies alias into low ones, the same effect that makes wagon wheels spin backwards on film. Because prior work down-scaled in the continuous domain, there was no natural place to insert this filter. Getting it wrong is precisely what produces the residual error.

zh.caption: 图1 为什么普通 CNN 只是近似尺度等变。把一张高分辨率数字和它「理想降采样」后的版本送进同一个 CNN，得到的两张特征图并不一致（上、下两路，红叉标出）。我们真正想要的是反过来成立：对高分辨率特征做降采样，应当精确还原出直接由低分辨率输入算得的特征。构造一个满足这一点的网络，正是本文的目标。

zh.text: 问题：不够精确的「等变」

尺度等变的意思是：如果你缩放输入，网络的内部特征会以对应方式一起变换，而最终类别保持不变。近期的尺度等变网络，比如 SESN、DSS、DISCO，都通过跨尺度共享权重来追求这一点：同一个核缩放后作用在每个尺度上。在连续域里看，这个思路很干净。但真实图像活在离散网格上，连续核必须被采样，而这一采样又把连续数学从不需要操心的混叠（aliasing）重新引了回来。结果就是一个可测量的等变误差，在论文的表格里大约是零点几，这意味着这些方法所宣称的保证，实际上只近似成立。
论文的诊断是：缺失的关键一环是抗混叠。奈奎斯特采样定理（Nyquist sampling theorem）指出，当你对离散信号降采样时，必须先去掉更粗网格已无法表示的那些频率；跳过这一步，高频就会混叠进低频，就像电影里马车轮子看上去在倒转的那种效应。因为此前的工作是在连续域里做降采样的，就没有一个自然的位置来插入这个滤波器。而没把它处理对，恰恰就是那个残余误差的来源。

en.title: NeurIPS 2023: Making Deep Nets Truly Scale-Equivariant, With Zero Error
en.subtitle: Purdue University rebuilds every network layer in the Fourier domain so that resizing an image and running the network commute exactly, not just approximately.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 让网络对尺度变化「真正」等变，误差精确为零
zh.subtitle: 普渡大学用 Fourier 层重建每一层网络，使「缩放图像」和「跑网络」两个操作严格可交换，而不再只是近似成立

en.text: The idea: define down-scaling correctly, then obey one frequency rule

The authors start by pinning down what down-scaling should mean. They define it as ideal downsampling: first apply an ideal low-pass filter that zeros out every frequency above the new grid's Nyquist limit, then subsample. Figure 2 shows this filtering as a pointwise product in the frequency domain, where the filter keeps a band of low frequencies and discards the rest. With this definition in hand, the anti-aliasing is no longer an afterthought bolted onto a continuous derivation; it is the very definition of the operation the network must be equivariant to.

en.caption: Figure 2. Ideal downsampling as frequency-domain filtering. The signal spectrum X is multiplied pointwise by an ideal low-pass filter H that is 1 on a band of low frequencies and 0 elsewhere, leaving only the retained low frequencies (H ⊙ X). Removing the high frequencies before subsampling is exactly the anti-aliasing step that prior continuous-domain formulations had no place for.

en.text: From this definition the paper derives its central condition, stated as Claim 1: a deep net is scale-equivariant under ideal downsampling if and only if every output frequency depends only on input frequencies that are equal or lower. Intuitively, information may flow from low frequencies up to high ones but never the other way, so that discarding the high band commutes with running the layer. This single rule, one output frequency reads only equal-or-lower input frequencies, becomes the design constraint that every layer must satisfy.

zh.text: 核心思路：先把降采样定义对，再服从一条频率规则
作者先把「降采样到底该是什么」钉死。他们将其定义为理想降采样（ideal downsampling）：先施加一个理想低通滤波器，把高于新网格奈奎斯特上限的所有频率清零，然后再抽样。图2 把这个滤波画成频域里的逐点相乘——滤波器保留一段低频、丢掉其余部分。有了这个定义，抗混叠就不再是补在连续推导后面的马后炮，而正是网络所要等变的那个操作的定义本身。

zh.caption: 图2 理想降采样即频域滤波。信号频谱 X 与一个理想低通滤波器 H 逐点相乘，H 在一段低频上取 1、其余处取 0，最终只留下被保留的低频（H ⊙ X）。在抽样之前先去掉高频，正是此前连续域方法无处安放的那一步抗混叠。

zh.text: 由这个定义出发，论文推导出它的核心条件，即 Claim 1：在理想降采样下，一个深度网络尺度等变，当且仅当每个输出频率只依赖于相等或更低的输入频率。直观地说，信息可以从低频流向高频，但绝不能反过来，这样一来「丢掉高频」这一步就能和「跑这一层」相交换。这条唯一的规则——一个输出频率只读取相等或更低的输入频率——就成了每一层都必须满足的设计约束。

en.title: NeurIPS 2023: Making Deep Nets Truly Scale-Equivariant, With Zero Error
en.subtitle: Purdue University rebuilds every network layer in the Fourier domain so that resizing an image and running the network commute exactly, not just approximately.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 让网络对尺度变化「真正」等变，误差精确为零
zh.subtitle: 普渡大学用 Fourier 层重建每一层网络，使「缩放图像」和「跑网络」两个操作严格可交换，而不再只是近似成立

en.text: A cat is a cat whether it fills the frame or sits far away as a handful of pixels. We would like a vision network to behave the same way: shrink the object, and the features should shrink with it, while the predicted label stays put. This property is called scale-equivariance, and a line of scale-equivariant CNNs has pursued it by sharing weights across a bank of resized kernels. The catch is subtle but consequential. These methods are derived on paper in the continuous domain and only later discretized for a real, pixel-grid implementation, and that discretization step leaks. What comes out is a network that is approximately scale-equivariant, carrying a small but stubborn error that never quite reaches zero.

A NeurIPS 2023 paper from Purdue University argues that the residual error is not a tuning problem but a modeling one. Down-scaling a discrete signal is a signal-processing operation, and signal processing has a hard rule for it: before you throw away samples, you must low-pass filter, or high frequencies fold down into low ones and corrupt the result. The continuous-domain formulations simply had no place for that anti-aliasing filter. The paper's fix is to formulate down-scaling directly in the discrete domain, with anti-aliasing built in from the first line, and then to rebuild every network component as a Fourier layer that respects it. The payoff is a family of deep nets that is truly scale-equivariant, with an end-to-end equivariance error of exactly zero, by construction rather than by luck.

en.caption: Figure 1. Why ordinary CNNs are only approximately scale-equivariant. Feed a high-resolution digit and its ideally down-scaled version through the same CNN and the two feature maps disagree (top vs. bottom, red cross). The property we actually want is the reverse: down-scaling a high-resolution feature should recover exactly the feature computed from the low-resolution input. Building a network where that holds is the paper's goal.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02922  |  Code: https://github.com/ashiq24/Scale_Equivarinat_Fourier_Layer
Takeaway

The lasting lesson is to treat scale-equivariance as a signal-processing problem. Once you define down-scaling as ideal, anti-aliased downsampling and require every output frequency to read only equal-or-lower input frequencies, you can assemble a network from Fourier layers that is exactly scale-equivariant, with provably zero error instead of the small residuals that trailed earlier methods.

The guarantee is not bought with accuracy. The model matches or beats prior scale-equivariant CNNs and is markedly more data-efficient, with the largest gains showing up on the harder natural-image setting. It is worth being precise about the boundary, though: the exact-zero guarantee lives in the ideal-downsampling regime, where theory and implementation coincide. Under non-ideal downsampling, when the anti-aliasing filter is imperfect and Gibbs ringing creeps in, a small error returns, even if the model still comes out ahead of every baseline.

More broadly, the paper is a reminder that many of the "approximate" equivariances in deep learning are approximate only because a fundamentally discrete operation was modeled as if it were continuous, and then discretized after the fact. Treating the operation the network must respect as a genuine signal-processing step, with anti-aliasing built in from the start rather than patched in at the end, is what converts an approximate symmetry into an exact one. The same recipe, define the discrete operation correctly and then constrain every layer to commute with it, may well carry over to the many other transformations that deep networks are routinely asked to respect.
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02922  |  Code: https://github.com/ashiq24/Scale_Equivarinat_Fourier_Layer

en.title: NeurIPS 2023: Making Deep Nets Truly Scale-Equivariant, With Zero Error
en.subtitle: Purdue University rebuilds every network layer in the Fourier domain so that resizing an image and running the network commute exactly, not just approximately.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 让网络对尺度变化「真正」等变，误差精确为零
zh.subtitle: 普渡大学用 Fourier 层重建每一层网络，使「缩放图像」和「跑网络」两个操作严格可交换，而不再只是近似成立

en.text: Results: exactly zero error, and it helps most where it is hardest

The model is evaluated on the two standard scale-equivariance benchmarks, MNIST-scale (resolutions from 8×8 up to 28×28) and STL10-scale (48 up to 97), against baselines including SESN, DSS, SI-CovNet, SS-CNN, DISCO, and a plain Fourier CNN. On MNIST-scale under ideal downsampling with all scales, it reaches 0.9889 accuracy and 0.9716 scale-consistency, the best on every metric, and, crucially, an equivariance error of exactly 0.00 where strong baselines like DISCO still register around 0.44. The zero is not a rounding artifact; it is guaranteed by the construction.

en.caption: Table 1. MNIST-scale accuracy, scale-consistency, and equivariance error under ideal downsampling (all scales). The proposed model leads on every metric, and its equivariance error is exactly zero by construction while the strongest baselines retain a measurable residual.

en.text: The advantage widens on the harder benchmark. On STL10-scale, natural color images where approximate methods struggle, the model reaches 0.7332 accuracy against 0.5844 for the next-best Fourier CNN, a gain of roughly 15 points, again with zero equivariance error. It also degrades gracefully under non-ideal downsampling, where the anti-aliasing filter is imperfect and Gibbs ringing appears: even there it stays the best model at 0.9880 accuracy, 0.9760 scale-consistency, and a small 0.05 error. And it is the most data-efficient of the group, reaching 0.9606 accuracy with just 1,000 training samples on MNIST-scale versus DISCO's 0.9457.

A feature visualization gives a sense of what the equivariant layers actually learn. Across both ideal and non-ideal downsampling, the model's feature maps trace spatially local structure, the contours and edges of each digit, rather than the diffuse, resolution-dependent patterns an ordinary CNN produces. The spatially-local Fourier convolution is doing what it was designed to do.

en.caption: Figure 3. Learned features under ideal (top rows) and non-ideal (bottom) downsampling. From the input digit the model produces feature maps that highlight spatially local structure, digit contours and edges, in both settings, evidence that the spatially-local Fourier convolution keeps a CNN-like inductive bias while remaining exactly scale-equivariant.

zh.text: 结果：误差精确为零，且越难的场景收益越大

模型在两个标准尺度等变基准上评测：MNIST-scale（分辨率从 8×8 到 28×28）和 STL10-scale（从 48 到 97），对比的基线包括 SESN、DSS、SI-CovNet、SS-CNN、DISCO 以及一个普通的 Fourier CNN。在理想降采样、覆盖全部尺度的 MNIST-scale 上，它取得 0.9889 的准确率和 0.9716 的尺度一致性，在每一项指标上都最好；而最关键的是，等变误差精确为 0.00，而 DISCO 这样的强基线仍有约 0.44。这个零不是四舍五入的结果，而是由构造保证的。

zh.caption: 表1 理想降采样（全部尺度）下 MNIST-scale 的准确率、尺度一致性与等变误差。本文模型在每一项指标上领先，其等变误差由构造精确为零，而最强的基线仍保留可测量的残余误差。

zh.text: 在更难的基准上，这个优势进一步拉开。在 STL10-scale 这个近似方法普遍吃力的自然彩色图像基准上，模型取得 0.7332 的准确率，而次好的 Fourier CNN 只有 0.5844，领先约 15 个百分点，且等变误差依然为零。它在非理想降采样下也退化得很平缓：当抗混叠滤波器不完美、出现 Gibbs 振铃时，它仍是最好的模型，准确率 0.9880、尺度一致性 0.9760，误差仅 0.05。它还是这组方法里最省数据的：在 MNIST-scale 上仅用 1000 个训练样本就达到 0.9606 的准确率，而 DISCO 为 0.9457。
一组特征可视化让人直观看到这些等变层到底学到了什么。无论理想还是非理想降采样，模型的特征图都勾勒出空间局部的结构——每个数字的轮廓和边缘，而不是普通 CNN 产生的那种弥散、依赖分辨率的图案。空间局部 Fourier 卷积确实在做它被设计出来要做的事。

zh.caption: 图3 理想（上方各行）与非理想（下方）降采样下学到的特征。从输入数字出发，模型在两种设定下都产生突出空间局部结构——数字轮廓与边缘——的特征图，说明空间局部 Fourier 卷积在保持精确尺度等变的同时，保留了类似 CNN 的归纳偏置。

Across both ideal and non-ideal downsampling, the model's feature maps trace spatially local structure, the contours and edges of each digit, rather than the diffuse, resolution-dependent patterns an ordinary CNN produces. The spatially-local Fourier convolution is doing what it was designed to do.

en.caption: Figure 3. Learned features under ideal (top rows) and non-ideal (bottom) downsampling. From the input digit the model produces feature maps that highlight spatially local structure, digit contours and edges, in both settings, evidence that the spatially-local Fourier convolution keeps a CNN-like inductive bias while remaining exactly scale-equivariant.

en.text: Takeaway

The lasting lesson is to treat scale-equivariance as a signal-processing problem. Once you define down-scaling as ideal, anti-aliased downsampling and require every output frequency to read only equal-or-lower input frequencies, you can assemble a network from Fourier layers that is exactly scale-equivariant, with provably zero error instead of the small residuals that trailed earlier methods.

The guarantee is not bought with accuracy. The model matches or beats prior scale-equivariant CNNs and is markedly more data-efficient, with the largest gains showing up on the harder natural-image setting. It is worth being precise about the boundary, though: the exact-zero guarantee lives in the ideal-downsampling regime, where theory and implementation coincide. Under non-ideal downsampling, when the anti-aliasing filter is imperfect and Gibbs ringing creeps in, a small error returns, even if the model still comes out ahead of every baseline.

More broadly, the paper is a reminder that many of the "approximate" equivariances in deep learning are approximate only because a fundamentally discrete operation was modeled as if it were continuous, and then discretized after the fact. Treating the operation the network must respect as a genuine signal-processing step, with anti-aliasing built in from the start rather than patched in at the end, is what converts an approximate symmetry into an exact one. The same recipe, define the discrete operation correctly and then constrain every layer to commute with it, may well carry over to the many other transformations that deep networks are routinely asked to respect.

zh.text: 结果：误差精确为零，且越难的场景收益越大

模型在两个标准尺度等变基准上评测：MNIST-scale（分辨率从 8×8 到 28×28）和 STL10-scale（从 48 到 97），对比的基线包括 SESN、DSS、SI-CovNet、SS-CNN、DISCO 以及一个普通的 Fourier CNN。在理想降采样、覆盖全部尺度的 MNIST-scale 上，它取得 0.9889 的准确率和 0.9716 的尺度一致性，在每一项指标上都最好；而最关键的是，等变误差精确为 0.00，而 DISCO 这样的强基线仍有约 0.44。这个零不是四舍五入的结果，而是由构造保证的。

zh.caption: 表1 理想降采样（全部尺度）下 MNIST-scale 的准确率、尺度一致性与等变误差。本文模型在每一项指标上领先，其等变误差由构造精确为零，而最强的基线仍保留可测量的残余误差。

zh.text: 在更难的基准上，这个优势进一步拉开。在 STL10-scale 这个近似方法普遍吃力的自然彩色图像基准上，模型取得 0.7332 的准确率，而次好的 Fourier CNN 只有 0.5844，领先约 15 个百分点，且等变误差依然为零。它在非理想降采样下也退化得很平缓：当抗混叠滤波器不完美、出现 Gibbs 振铃时，它仍是最好的模型，准确率 0.9880、尺度一致性 0.9760，误差仅 0.05。它还是这组方法里最省数据的：在 MNIST-scale 上仅用 1000 个训练样本就达到 0.9606 的准确率，而 DISCO 为 0.9457。
一组特征可视化让人直观看到这些等变层到底学到了什么。无论理想还是非理想降采样，模型的特征图都勾勒出空间局部的结构——每个数字的轮廓和边缘，而不是普通 CNN 产生的那种弥散、依赖分辨率的图案。空间局部 Fourier 卷积确实在做它被设计出来要做的事。

zh.caption: 图3 理想（上方各行）与非理想（下方）降采样下学到的特征。从输入数字出发，模型在两种设定下都产生突出空间局部结构——数字轮廓与边缘——的特征图，说明空间局部 Fourier 卷积在保持精确尺度等变的同时，保留了类似 CNN 的归纳偏置。

zh.text: 结语

最值得记住的一点是：把尺度等变当作一个信号处理问题来对待。一旦你把降采样定义为理想的、带抗混叠的降采样，并要求每个输出频率只读取相等或更低的输入频率，就能用 Fourier 层拼出一个精确尺度等变的网络——误差在可证明的意义上为零，而不是像早期方法那样拖着一条小尾巴。而且这个保证并非以准确率为代价换来：模型追平或超过此前的尺度等变 CNN，并且明显更省数据，收益最大的恰是更难的自然图像场景。需要如实说明的边界是：精确为零的保证成立于理想降采样这一设定；在非理想降采样下会回来一个小误差，尽管模型依然领先。把离散信号处理这一步做对，正是把近似等变变成精确等变的关键。

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 让网络对尺度变化「真正」等变，误差精确为零
zh.subtitle: 普渡大学用 Fourier 层重建每一层网络，使「缩放图像」和「跑网络」两个操作严格可交换，而不再只是近似成立

en.caption: Figure 1. Why ordinary CNNs are only approximately scale-equivariant. Feed a high-resolution digit and its ideally down-scaled version through the same CNN and the two feature maps disagree (top vs. bottom, red cross). The property we actually want is the reverse: down-scaling a high-resolution feature should recover exactly the feature computed from the low-resolution input. Building a network where that holds is the paper's goal.

en.text: Ablation: the consistency loss earns its place

To check that the consistency loss is doing real work rather than riding along, the authors remove it and retrain at several training-set sizes. Both accuracy and scale-consistency drop at every size: at 5,000 samples scale-consistency falls from 0.9296 to 0.9150, and at 2,500 samples from 0.8906 to 0.8633. The loss reliably improves scale-consistent behavior, which is why it stays in the final recipe. The authors also report that applying the non-linearity directly in the frequency domain, though it preserves equivariance, hurt classification, which is why they use a spatial-domain scale-equivariant non-linearity instead.

zh.caption: 图1 为什么普通 CNN 只是近似尺度等变。把一张高分辨率数字和它「理想降采样」后的版本送进同一个 CNN，得到的两张特征图并不一致（上、下两路，红叉标出）。我们真正想要的是反过来成立：对高分辨率特征做降采样，应当精确还原出直接由低分辨率输入算得的特征。构造一个满足这一点的网络，正是本文的目标。

zh.text: 消融：一致性损失确实有用

为验证一致性损失是在真正起作用、而不是搭个便车，作者把它去掉后在若干训练集规模上重训。准确率和尺度一致性在每个规模上都下降：5000 个样本时尺度一致性从 0.9296 掉到 0.9150，2500 个样本时从 0.8906 掉到 0.8633。这项损失稳定地改善了尺度一致性行为，因此保留在最终配方中。作者还指出，如果把非线性直接放到频域里施加，虽然能保持等变，却会损害分类效果，这也是他们改用空间域尺度等变非线性的原因。

en.subtitle: Purdue University rebuilds every network layer in the Fourier domain so that resizing an image and running the network commute exactly, not just approximately.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 让网络对尺度变化「真正」等变，误差精确为零
zh.subtitle: 普渡大学用 Fourier 层重建每一层网络，使「缩放图像」和「跑网络」两个操作严格可交换，而不再只是近似成立

en.caption: Figure 3. Learned features under ideal (top rows) and non-ideal (bottom) downsampling. From the input digit the model produces feature maps that highlight spatially local structure, digit contours and edges, in both settings, evidence that the spatially-local Fourier convolution keeps a CNN-like inductive bias while remaining exactly scale-equivariant.

en.text: The problem: equivariance that isn't quite exact

Scale-equivariance means that if you resize the input, the network's internal features transform in the corresponding way and the final label is unchanged. Recent scale-equivariant networks, such as SESN, DSS, and DISCO, chase this by weight-sharing across scales: the same kernel, resized, is applied at each scale. Derived in the continuous domain, the idea is clean. But real images live on a discrete grid, so the continuous kernels have to be sampled, and that sampling reintroduces exactly the aliasing the continuous math never had to worry about. The result is a measurable equivariance error, on the order of a few tenths in the paper's tables, which means the guarantee these methods advertise holds only approximately.

The paper's diagnosis is that the missing ingredient is anti-aliasing. The Nyquist sampling theorem says that when you subsample a discrete signal, you must first remove the frequencies that the coarser grid can no longer represent; skip that step and those high frequencies alias into low ones, the same effect that makes wagon wheels spin backwards on film. Because prior work down-scaled in the continuous domain, there was no natural place to insert this filter. Getting it wrong is precisely what produces the residual error.

zh.text: 一只猫无论占满整个画面，还是远处几个像素的小点，它都还是一只猫。我们希望视觉网络也能这样：物体缩小，提取到的特征应当随之缩小，而预测出的类别保持不变。这一性质叫做尺度等变（scale-equivariance）。一类尺度等变 CNN 为此在一组不同尺寸的卷积核之间共享权重，用「同一个核、缩放到不同尺度」的方式来逼近它。问题很微妙但影响不小：这些方法是在连续域（continuous domain）里推导出来的，真正落到像素网格上实现时才做离散化，而离散化这一步会「漏」。最终得到的网络只是近似尺度等变，始终带着一个不大却顽固、怎么调都到不了零的误差。

普渡大学发表在 NeurIPS 2023 的这篇论文提出，这个残余误差不是调参问题，而是建模问题。对离散信号做降采样本质上是一次信号处理操作，而信号处理对此有一条硬规则：在丢弃采样点之前必须先做低通滤波，否则高频会「折叠」进低频、污染结果。连续域的推导里根本没有给这个抗混叠（anti-aliasing）滤波器留位置。论文的做法是：直接在离散域里定义降采样，从第一步就把抗混叠内建进去，再把网络的每一个组件都重建成遵守这条规则的 Fourier 层。回报是一族真正尺度等变的深度网络，端到端等变误差精确为零，靠的是构造本身而不是运气。

zh.caption: 图1 为什么普通 CNN 只是近似尺度等变。把一张高分辨率数字和它「理想降采样」后的版本送进同一个 CNN，得到的两张特征图并不一致（上、下两路，红叉标出）。我们真正想要的是反过来成立：对高分辨率特征做降采样，应当精确还原出直接由低分辨率输入算得的特征。构造一个满足这一点的网络，正是本文的目标。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02922  |  代码：https://github.com/ashiq24/Scale_Equivarinat_Fourier_Layer
